$comment: One set of load modes for every under-load harness, so numbers compare (cmuxterm-hq
docs/design/chat-instant-under-load.md, 'The bench': 'One harness, one set of load modes, used by typing and by
the tab and workspace harness, so numbers compare'). Leo, 2026-11-16: 'but typing under load is not good
Read by webviews/bench/loadModes.ts (the page-harness helpers) and by scripts/cmux-next/typing-frame-bench.py
(the native typing surfaces). Neither hard-codes a mode: a mode added here is offered by both. The web
composer typing bench (composer-typing.bench.ts, cmux-bench `typing`) keeps its own L0-L3 in composer-load.ts.
`web` is what a page harness applies; `native` is what the app harness applies. A knob a harness cannot express
is listed in that harness's `missing`, and the harness prints it beside the row, so a number is never read as
the full mode (a webview page has no terminals or workspaces). `native.rows` is the focused agent chat's
transcript: the native harness seeds that many rows into it (debug.agent_pane seed_rows) before it streams.
`gate_p95_ms` is the design's target for key to frame (16 ms, 8.3 hoped for). It is a bench flag
(--gate-p95-ms), not a CI gate (written under the 2026-10-23 no-new-CI rule, since lifted).
